solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Characters in this pub breaking a wobbly table (8)

indicators.note: PH breaks into the other letters, splitting them
a wobbly table is unsteady, its letters shaken loose

blocks.note: taken as it stands
PH = public house, the map abbreviation
TABLE rearranged; PH goes in after the L

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub notices writing on a rickety table.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the clue itself: every character printed in it comes from the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the full set of characters from which this clue, like any English text, is written.

clue.text: Support band member missing intro (6)

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a bass player in a band
BASSIST without its B

explanation.surface: A support band turns up without the player who starts the song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support band' reads as one phrase, the opening act at a gig; the definition is 'Support' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean giving help, whether with a hand or with money.

clue.text: First page about Homer stimulated influential output (9)

indicators.note: P ONE goes round the other letters
HOMER is stirred up into a new order

blocks.note: page one, P ONE, is the first page
HOMER rearranged, placed inside P ONE

explanation.surface: An opening page about Homer has fired up a hugely influential body of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Output' and 'First page' suggest books and literary influence, but the output is a chemical one secreted by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheromone is a chemical an animal gives off that influences the behaviour of others of its species.

clue.text: Quiz expert grasping point with suspicion (7)

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tight in the hand, so ACE holds N within it

blocks.note: to quiz is to ask
an ace is an expert
N = north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A quiz champion is holding a point of view with some distrust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiz expert' reads as one person, a quiz champion; it is two pieces, ASK then ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look with suspicion or disapproval.

clue.text: Delicate foxtrot involved in line dancing (5)

indicators.note: F is taken into the other letters
the letters of LINE move about

blocks.note: Foxtrot is F in the NATO alphabet
anagram fodder, with F worked in

explanation.surface: A dainty foxtrot turns up in a line-dancing class.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all dance floor, foxtrot and line dancing, which hides that the foxtrot is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: Film director’s sources reported (6)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: wells are sources of water

explanation.surface: A news item names where a film director got his information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sources reported' suggests a journalist's informants, but the sources are water wells. The ’s is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Death tally rising — no hospital present locally (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising reads the word from bottom to top
'no hospital' means without the hospital, so its letter H is taken out of the word

blocks.note: death is the end
to tally is to agree, to chime
CHIME without H, the hospital sign

explanation.surface: The death toll climbs in a place with no hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tally' looks like a count of deaths; it is the verb, to agree or chime.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease is endemic when it is regularly found in a particular area.

clue.text: Wild clip’s content with short film (5)

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inside letters
the word is cut off before its end

blocks.note: the inside of cLIp
VIDEO cut short

explanation.surface: Something outrageous is in a video clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' sits next to 'clip' as if describing it; it is the definition, meaning furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild in its angry sense, 'he went wild', which is what livid means in everyday speech.

clue.text: Novelist in South Africa to remain alive for now (8)

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
to linger is to hang on, still alive for the time being

explanation.surface: A writer is staying on in South Africa for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a novelist's travel plans; 'in' here is just the charade's joint, SA then LINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger wrote The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Traitress going for hotel chain? (8)

blocks.note: a traitress is a she-rat, a female rat or betrayer
on = going, as in 'the show is on'

explanation.surface: A female traitor is off to a chain of hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going for' reads as heading to; 'going' gives ON and 'for' joins the wordplay to the definition. The question mark flags the playful SHE-RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, hence the question mark: Sheraton is one hotel chain among many, run by Marriott.

clue.text: Welcome subject of discussion? (5,2,3,5)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a topic people are glad to talk about
the meant reading: 'welcome' as a verb, greeting the person who was just being talked about as they walk in

explanation.surface: A greeting offered to the very person everyone was just talking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcome' looks like an adjective, a pleasant topic; it is the verb, a greeting to someone who walks in just as they are being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: People say 'speak of the devil' when the person they were talking about appears.

clue.text: Under oath, exhausted, admitted to offence (5,2)

indicators.note: to be admitted to a place is to be let inside it, so WORN goes inside SIN

blocks.note: a sin is an offence
worn out, exhausted

explanation.surface: A tired witness, under oath, confesses to a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom surface makes 'admitted to offence' look like a confession; it is WORN admitted into SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sworn in has formally taken an oath, so is under oath.

clue.text: Beastly male duck turning in fast time (7)

indicators.note: NADA turns round to read backwards

blocks.note: a male sheep, a male beast
duck = nothing (a cricket score of nought), and nada is nothing

explanation.surface: A male animal and a duck are spinning round very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast time' looks like speed; it is a time of fasting. A duck is a batsman's score of nought in cricket, so nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Street location’s place to a certain river’s east (8)

indicators.note: SET is attached to the earlier letters
in an across entry, east is to the right, so SET comes after

blocks.note: 'some' as in 'some person' = a certain person
the standard abbreviation
to set is to place

explanation.surface: Directions for finding a street by its position east of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is a town in Somerset, a county in south-west England, home of Clarks shoes. The capital S is hidden by starting the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Street lies in the English county of Somerset.

clue.text: Dismal end for beggar: nothing in hat (8)

indicators.note: take the last letter of the word

blocks.note: sombre = gloomy, dismal
the last letter of beggaR
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A beggar's sad end: not a coin in his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The beggar's hat looks like the collecting cap with nothing in it; 'in' only joins the wordplay to 'hat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Seek ornament with engraving (5)

blocks.note: to seek as a pursuer does, running after a quarry
the metalworker's verb for engraving or embossing silver

explanation.surface: An instruction to go after decoration with carved lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the metalworker's verb: to chase silver is to engrave or emboss it.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to seek, and also to decorate metal by engraving.

clue.text: Orchestra sacks leader! Great man, and loyal! (9)

indicators.note: the first letter is sacked

blocks.note: the HALLE, the Manchester orchestra, without its H
a giant is a great man

explanation.surface: An orchestra fires its principal violinist, and players praise a great and faithful man.
explanation.walkthrough: An orchestra's leader is its principal violinist, but here it is the first letter. The Hallé is an orchestra based in Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiant means showing allegiance, loyal.

clue.text: Is obliged to cross road in difficulty (8)

indicators.note: HAS goes across RD, taking it inside

blocks.note: as in 'she has to go'
the address abbreviation
in = fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: Someone has to get across the road while in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In difficulty' reads as a phrase; 'in' is wordplay, meaning trendy, and 'difficulty' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a trying situation, as in 'suffering financial hardship'.

clue.text: King on fantastic British bitter (5)

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing 'on' another is placed next to it, so R is tacked on to ACE

blocks.note: ace = excellent, fantastic
R = rex, Latin for king
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A monarch praises a superb British bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British bitter' looks like the beer; bitter is the adjective, sour-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare form of acerbic, meaning bitter or sour.

clue.text: Old PM in undisguised triumph (7)

blocks.note: a bald statement is plain and undisguised
a win is a triumph

explanation.surface: A former prime minister enjoys an open victory.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was British Prime Minister three times between the wars. 'In' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin was a UK Prime Minister in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Liberal in Crown dependency rebuked youngster (3-5)

indicators.note: 'Liberal in' places the Liberal inside what follows, so L sits within CHID

blocks.note: the Isle of Man is a Crown dependency
chid is the old past tense of chide
the party abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Liberal on a small island scolded a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: A Crown dependency is a self-governing island under the British Crown, such as the Isle of Man or Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal, old-fashioned sense of man-child, a boy, rather than the modern one of an immature adult.

clue.text: Weapon to keep animals together outside a pound (7)

indicators.note: the herd stands outside, around, the other letters, so HERD wraps A LB

blocks.note: to herd is to gather animals
taken as it stands
lb, the abbreviation for pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone uses a weapon to keep livestock together just outside an animal pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests an enclosure for stray animals, fitting the herding picture; it is the weight, LB.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a combined spear and battleaxe.

clue.text: Long-dead Roman disrupted seance (6)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman's spirit breaks up a seance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a ghost story, a long-dead figure disrupting a seance, which makes the definition look like a spirit being summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca was a Roman philosopher and dramatist who died in AD 65.

clue.text: Ambition shown by learner nurtured by the German engineer (7)

indicators.note: AIM L is held and cared for within DER

blocks.note: der is German for 'the'
an aim is an ambition
L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A young German engineer, taken under someone's wing, shows ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The German' is the article, DER, not a person; 'shown by' just joins AIM to L.
explanation.definitionFit: Gottlieb Daimler was a German engineer and motor-car pioneer.

clue.text: Died in a Murdoch’s embrace in Elba? (5)

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so IRIS wraps round D

blocks.note: Iris Murdoch, the novelist
the standard abbreviation, as in dates

explanation.surface: Someone dies in a Murdoch's arms on the island of Elba.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba looks like Napoleon's island of exile; the question mark shows it is a definition by example, the actor Idris Elba.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris is the first name of the actor Idris Elba.

clue.text: Marker pens keep record of Rhineland city (7)

indicators.note: to pen animals is to shut them in, so CONE shuts LOG inside it

blocks.note: a traffic cone marks off road
to log is to keep a record

explanation.surface: Some marker pens are used to keep records in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marker pens' reads as one noun, felt-tips; 'Marker' is the cone and 'pens' is the verb, enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a city on the Rhine in western Germany.

clue.text: Smart female copper Bond supports (5)

indicators.note: in a down entry, TIE sits under CU, holding it up

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: A clever policewoman backs up James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female copper' reads as a policewoman, and 'Bond' as the spy; the definition is 'Smart female', someone attractive and clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive, often clever-seeming woman.

clue.text: Rebel woman’s English protégé cut down in kidnap? (8,3,4)

indicators.note: 'cut down in kidnap' puts the felling inside the seizing, so HEW sits within TAKE

blocks.note: her = belonging to a woman
the standard abbreviation
a ward is someone under another's protection
to take someone is to seize them
to hew is to cut down, as with trees

explanation.surface: A rebellious woman's English protégé is killed during an abduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake led English resistance to the Norman conquest in the Fens in the 1070s.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward the Wake was an Anglo-Saxon rebel against William the Conqueror.

clue.text: Stink surrounds second one putting on act (6)

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so PONG encloses S I

blocks.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell
the standard abbreviation
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a fuss about the runner-up showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stink' reads as a fuss, as in 'kick up a stink'; it is a smell, PONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Posing in its sense of pretending or showing off, as a poseur does, rather than sitting for a portrait.

clue.text: Archdeacon and defaulter reportedly prolonged dispute (8)

indicators.note: the word is taken by how it sounds when reported

blocks.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
a debtor who fails to pay is a defaulter; non-rhotic DEBTOR

explanation.surface: A church official and a man who won't pay up are locked in a long feud.
explanation.walkthrough: Archdeacons in the Church of England carry the title 'the Venerable'. DETTA matches DEBTOR only in a British accent that drops the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Italian for revenge: a blood feud passed between families, so long-running is built in.
